gameStory.articleHeadline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 150 receiving yards and a score in the Seahawks' 20-3 win over the Chiefs
gameStory.articleDescription: — Frustrated by a two-game skid, the Seattle Seahawks went into playoff mode.
gameStory.articleStory: SEATTLE -- — Frustrated by a two-game skid, the Seattle Seahawks went into playoff mode. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, and the Seahawks handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the season, 20-3 on Sunday night. Sam Darnold threw for 257 yards and a score for the Seahawks (4-3), while Emanuel Wilson had 24 carries for 100 yards and a TD. “Playing a team like Kansas City and all the killers that they got on that side, we knew how big this game was, and we wanted this one badly,” said Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver and reigning Offensive Player of the Year. “You know, we saw it as a playoff game.” Patrick Mahomes struggled, throwing for 165 yards with an interception for the Chiefs (5-1). Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks last season before signing with the Chiefs in the offseason, was held to 36 yards on 14 carries. Walker entered the night averaging a league-leading 133 yards per game, but the Seahawks shut him down, along with the rest of Kansas City's offense. The Chiefs had 213 total yards, 50 on the ground. “Listen, all three phases we struggled, so we’ve got to do better, and that’s my responsibility,” Kansas City coach Andy Reid said. “So I take full responsibility for this. whatToWatch.text: Snap the skid at home: Seattle's 3-3 and riding a two-game losing streak, but they're 3-point favorites in their own building against Kansas City — this is exactly the kind of game that flips a season one way or the other.

Pass rush vs. a stingy defense: the Seahawks are getting home 2.7 times a game, nearly a full sack more per game than KC's 1.6 — and with the Chiefs allowing just 16.6 points a night, that pressure may be the difference-maker.

Low total, high stakes: a 43.5 over/under says oddsmakers expect a grinder, and with five players out on each side (Seattle without Connor O'Toole, Drew Lock and Beau Stephens; KC missing Garrett Nussmeier and Jack Pyburn), depth and execution decide this one.

recap.text: Seattle snapped a two-game slide in the loudest way possible, smothering previously unbeaten Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night. Jaxon Smith-Njigba torched the Chiefs secondary for 150 yards on nine grabs, including a 28-yard scoring strike from Sam Darnold that gave the Seahawks a second-quarter cushion they never surrendered. The defense did the rest, picking off Patrick Mahomes, holding Kenneth Walker III to 36 yards on 14 carries and limiting Kansas City to a lone Harrison Butker field goal. Emanuel Wilson slammed the door with a 21-yard touchdown run in the fourth, capping a 100-yard night on 24 carries and sending the Seahawks to 4-3.

newsBlurb.text: Seattle's backfield arrives at Lumen Field held together with tape: Jadarian Price remains parked on injured reserve, leaving Zach Charbonnet's availability as the week's biggest question mark against Kansas City. Mike Macdonald offered nothing on Charbonnet's progress, so the Seahawks may have to manufacture a run game against the Chiefs with whoever's standing. Few storylines carry more weight Sunday than who lines up behind center in the backfield.
